Subject: Post-demo: pilot decision path & hosted vs dedicated qualification

Samir / Elena — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our demo and a proposed next-steps checklist so we can lock the right deployment path: Hosted API vs Dedicated capacity vs Private VPC.

Key notes from the call (please confirm or correct):
- Primary workload: real-time suggestion endpoint for product search (synonyms + rerank).
- Peak QPS observed in pilot target: ~900 QPS (burst to 1.2k for <10 min).
- Typical prompt size: 60-100 tokens; tail requests up to ~450 tokens for complex conversational flows.
- Target SLOs: p95 latency <= 60ms for short requests (<=100 tokens); p95 below ~200ms for long-tail.
- Data concerns: no PHI, but must be behind corporate network for Prod (VPC option discussed).

Attachments: pilot-MVP-scope.pdf (scope + success metrics), capacity_profile.csv (sample QPS distribution)

Two decision paths we recommended on the call and my read:
1) Fast validation (recommended initial): Hosted API pilot configured with warm cache + traffic mirroring. Advantages: fastest to get real traffic, easy telemetry, streaming logs for eval. We'll watch tail latency and KV cache warmup.
2) Production scale (if pilot shows steady >800 QPS with strict p95): move to Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) with pinned model version and autoscale windows to guarantee throughput/latency.

Ask: could you confirm the numbers above (peak QPS, token distribution) and grant read-only access to a 24-48h traffic sample (anonymized) or a replay file? That will let us produce a short viability matrix (expected p95 vs config) and a pilot plan with estimated cost.

Proposed mutual action plan (MAP) — timeline for pilot (2–4 weeks):
- Day 0–2: Exchange traffic sample + define success metrics (p95, error-rate, cost/op).
- Day 3–7: Redwood sets up Hosted pilot with tracing, request-level cost telemetry, and a short warmup schedule (KV cache seeding).
- Week 2: Run 48h focused window with mirrored production traffic during peak window.
- Week 3: Review metrics and recommend Hosted->Dedicated cutover if sustained >800 QPS with <60ms p95.

Rough cost guidance (very rough): Hosted pilot (1–2 weeks with observed 900 QPS bursts): ~$6–12k of usage credits depending on token distribution. Dedicated reservation guidance will follow after traffic analysis.

I’ll follow up with a short qualification email for tradeoffs and technical knobs (batching, cache TTL, cold-starts, autoscale windows). If procurement wants to join the thread, happy to loop them in.

Thanks — Aditya

Samir — great, thanks for the numbers. Below is a concise qualification and the performance levers that will determine Hosted vs Dedicated fit.

Quick qualification summary:
- If peak sustained QPS is below ~800 with similar token distribution, Hosted + cache/continuous-batching will likely meet p95 <= 60ms for short requests.
- If sustained peaks are at/above ~900–1.2k with tight p95 requirements, Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs with pinned model + tuned batching) gives better headroom and guaranteed tail latency.

Technical tradeoffs (short):
- Batching: Hosted does continuous batching but with multi-tenant variability; Dedicated gives deterministic batching windows we can tune (batch-size cap, request coalescing).
- KV cache warmup: Short requests benefit heavily from prefix/KV cache; we can seed cache during pilot but production Dedicated makes cache placement predictable.
- Cold-starts & autoscale: Hosted scales quickly but may incur transient latency on sudden spikes; Dedicated with warm standby handles bursts with reserved throughput.
- Observability: Hosted pilot gives immediate access to token-level cost, traces, and per-route p95. Dedicated includes the same telemetry plus SLA-backed latency targets.

Proposed pilot plan (revised — 10 business days):
- Day 0: Access to 48h anonymized traffic replay and dev keys.
- Days 1–3: Redwood sets up Hosted pilot with: pinned model variant for pilot, KV cache seeding script, continuous batching target=8, instrumentation for p50/p95/p99 and QPS split.
- Days 4–7: Run mirrored traffic during your peak window(s). Collect metrics.
- Day 8: Joint review and recommendation: stay Hosted (optimize configs) vs transition plan to Dedicated.

Cost ballpark (pilot): Hosted usage credits estimate $8k–$14k depending on token churn and cache effectiveness. Dedicated estimate for production baseline (1x reserved pool sized for 1.2k sustained QPS) will be provided after traffic analysis — expect a monthly reserved commit.

Ask: please share the anonymized 48h replay or a sample of 100k requests (format: JSONL with token count and timestamp). If you prefer, we can run a small client-side replay that never leaves your network (we provide a dockerized harness).

If procurement is ready, we can include a short trial addendum (7–14 day trial + pilot credits) and a standard NDA.

Thanks — Aditya
